name: Dzando
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only surveys/comparative wordlists (Fultz & Morgan 2016; Hackett & van Bulck 1956); no grammar or phonology exists

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record dzan1238 (Dzando; dialects Lokay, Maboko, Moliba, Molunga; Bamweic).
sources.note: n/a — used to establish that Moliba is a Dzando dialect.

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. Thèse de doctorat, ULB/UGent.
sources.note: Nothing on Dzando: 'djândo' and 'moliba' appear only in the Kungu-territory language inventory table (p.~21); Dzando is not among the ten languages described.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2009. Le réseau fluvial congolais et la problématique des expansions bantoues. Annales Aequatoria 30: 839-988.
sources.note: Nothing; p.843-844 states explicitly that 'à l'intérieur même du triangle, il restait encore des langues à étudier : limpoko, gyándo-moliba, ndoolo, tanda, bombóli, likoká, bondzo, enyélé… (Motingea, 1996a: 5)' — i.e. Motingea 1996 (CNWS 43) does not describe Dzando either.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale (Études Aequatoria 8). Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria.
sources.note: Nothing on Dzando: p.12 lists 'GROUPE DE LA NGIRI / SOUS-GROUPE BAMWE: 1. Mônyâ 2. Gyando 3. Moliba [Ebuku-Lingonda] 4. Sombe [5. Lifonga].. [9. Libobi]' — only the bracketed parlers are sketched; Gyando (=Dzando) and Moliba are named but not described.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du Nord-Ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin IRCB 22(4): 900-919.
sources.note: Nothing; 'tonologie déplacée' of the Bangala-des-marais illustrated with Sombe (Bamwe); Dzandu/Moliba not named; tone only.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. De tonologie der naamwoorden te Ebuku. Kongo-Overzee 16(5): 281-291 (pp. 287-291 general comparison of the seven idioms).
sources.note: Nothing on Moliba/Dzando stress. p.288-289 'a. Te Moliba: Het naamwoord krijgt twee hoge begintonen wanneer het na een ander woord komt..'; p.291 a generic speculation that in some Bantu languages tone may have ceded its role 'aan lengte- of andere accenten', not applied to any of these languages.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. De tonologie der naamwoorden te Maleke-Moleke en Moliba. Kongo-Overzee 16(4): 212-223 (section F, 'De tonologie der naamwoorden te Moliba', pp. 217-223).
sources.note: Nothing. First-hand noun-tonology sketch of the Moliba dialect (informants from Bomole and Liboko, 'hoofdij Moliba.. sector der Dzandu, gewest Bomboma', p.218): H/L tone types, tone sandhi on following words, summary p.222-223 that the noun tone melody is 'regelmatig een klankgreep achteruit geschoven'. No mention of klemtoon/accent/nadruk/length anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. Eigenaardige toonstructuur van enkele Bantoetalen in het Noord-Westen van Belgisch-Kongo. Kongo-Overzee 16(1): 37-53.
sources.note: Nothing. Series introduction (Botoko baseline); fn.2 p.38 lists Moliba among the seven idioms treated as 'afzonderlijke talen of dialectgroepen'. Tone only; the only 'klemtoon' hit in the issue is Burssens' review of an Indonesian textbook.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1949. Dialectgroepen in het Ngiri-gebied. Aequatoria 12: 87-94.
sources.note: Nothing. p.94 table row 'v Dzandu-secteur — Dzandu, Moliba, n° 27, 28'; lexical isogloss-bundle counts only.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1948. Les classifications des langues en Afrique. Bulletin des séances de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge 19(4): 846-873.
sources.note: Nothing. p.858 list 'Nos 26-31. Bamwe, Dzandu, Muliba, Boniange, Ewaku, Monia'; p.868 'b) Les parlers des dzandu.. chefferies de Maboko, Lokay et Mlounga.. c) Les parlers des moliba, qui font aussi partie du secteur des Dzandu'. Classification and demography only.
sources.venue: Bulletin des séances de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge
